summary.text: A 4-week-old female neonate who first presented at 3 weeks of age with fever (Tmax 39.5 °C), irritability, poor feeding, decreased urine output and reduced movement of the left lower limb.

The initial workup included lumbar puncture, WBC 14 × 10⁹/L, neutrophils 6.7 × 10⁹/L and CRP 24 mg/L, negative blood, CSF and urine cultures, positive urinalysis leukocytes, respiratory PCR detecting human rhinovirus/enterovirus, and a small left-sided hip effusion on ultrasound. She was initially managed as neonatal sepsis and completed 7 days of intravenous ampicillin and cefotaxime.

One week later she re-presented with irritability and limited movement of the left hip. MRI findings were consistent with left hip septic arthritis and periarticular pyomyositis. Empirical intravenous ceftriaxone and vancomycin were initiated and she underwent left hip joint washout and drainage.

Blood and joint fluid cultures were negative but joint fluid PCR was positive for Bacteroides fragilis. Metronidazole was added and therapy was later streamlined to piperacillin-tazobactam to complete a total of 4 weeks of antimicrobial therapy from the date of surgical drainage.
